result:
A logged model's status message now survives the round trip to its serialized form and back. A failed model with "Upload failed" comes back with "Upload failed". The new test passes.

**Fix:** In `LoggedModel.to_proto` (`mlflow/entities/logged_model.py`), I added `status_message=self.status_message` to the info message next to `status`. Reading it back (`from_proto`) already worked; the value just was never being written. Nothing else changed.

**Test:** I added `tests/entities/test_logged_model.py`, since there was no test file for this class. It builds a failed model with "Upload failed", checks that the serialized form contains the message, and checks that reading it back gives the same status and message and an identical model overall.

The test also turned up a separate, existing quirk, which I left alone: a model created without metrics comes back with an empty metrics list instead of no metrics. The test sets metrics to an empty list to sidestep that.

+from mlflow.entities import LoggedModel, LoggedModelStatus
+
+
+def test_logged_model_proto_round_trip_preserves_status_message():
+    model = LoggedModel(
+        experiment_id="1",
+        model_id="m-123",
+        name="model",
+        artifact_location="file:///tmp/artifacts",
+        creation_timestamp=1,
+        last_updated_timestamp=2,
+        model_type="agent",
+        source_run_id="run-1",
+        status=LoggedModelStatus.FAILED,
+        status_message="Upload failed",
+        tags={"k": "v"},
+        params={"p": "1"},
+        metrics=[],
+    )
+
+    proto = model.to_proto()
+    assert proto.info.status_message == "Upload failed"
+
+    restored = LoggedModel.from_proto(proto)
+    assert restored.status == LoggedModelStatus.FAILED
+    assert restored.status_message == "Upload failed"
+    assert restored.to_dictionary() == model.to_dictionary()
